coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-eight attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 88eb2234 at 0444, 14368 bytes, unmoved; HEAD never left 5d5d778 and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head; required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified and matching their pins; all twelve recordedInputs files reproduce with basedOn cross-checked at zero disagreements. CLAUDE-G23LJ-V2-SF1 is landed. v2's predecessor role read 'Measured harness-spec and named-catalog leftoverDesign false' when v1 has no obligation containing catalog and no G23 catalog artifact exists; v3 reads 'named-corpus', which maps to OBL-G23-NAMED-CORPUS on frozen v1 alongside the two abbreviations that already mapped. The word catalog now occurs three times against v2's one, which on a raw count would look like the opposite of a repair, so I read all three: a refusal in purpose, the finding quoted in the predecessorV2 role, and findingDisposition stating that no catalog artifact is asserted. The count rose and the assertion disappeared. The repair is the tightest I have measured in this family. Six obligations in, six out, none added, none removed, and zero obligations modified in any field; only artifact, version, authorityClaim, basedOn, purpose and recordedInputs changed with findingDisposition added — exactly the surface a successor must move. doesNot is byte-identical at fifteen entries, summary.leftoverDesign is unchanged, and namedClassesThisGate remains NT-3 and NT-5. I also re-ran the probe that produced a SHOULD-FIX two reviews ago. basedOn.inputCorpus.role reads 'Named initial states from live exactByteIntent', the third consecutive subject carrying that byte-identical string — false at G18, true at G22, and true here: g23-input-corpus.v1 has four states, all with distinct stateNamed values, eight exactByteIntent occurrences, and all four sources citing it. Three subjects, three independent measurements. Boundaries hold at source. D-147's adopted text assigns DR-G23, gives it DR-133 NT-3 and NT-5 only, and closes their leftover-design with the remainder at G23 execution; the join states exactly that and reopens nothing. D-146 is recorded as a leftover-join of the NT grouping rather than of this OBL id, the distinction G23 v1's own leftoverNameNote draws. NT-1, NT-2, NT-4, NT-6, NT-7 and NT-8 appear in four fields between them and every occurrence is a refusal. Register checks: cell [7] of the DR-G23 row is OPEN and cell [4] is 'Protocol + semantic owners', byte-identical to liveGateOwners. Because CLAUDE-PTLJ-V3-SF1 was filed against a v3 whose version field read 2, I checked all three identity triples in this family: v1/1, v2/2 and v3/3 are all consistent. Disclosure: this repairs my own SHOULD-FIX, every Claude-lane verdict it pins is mine, and the identity test is my own finding. The hazard in a one-word repair is confirming the word and stopping, so I ran the full battery and the over-correction diff separately; the hazard in the recurring role string is settling into a previous answer, so I measured it from the corpus's own bytes a third time.
